sources.entry: DropPoint - Make drag-and-drop easier using DropPoint. Helps to drag content without having to open side-by-side windows.

summary.one_liner: DropPoint is a cross-platform Electron-style desktop tool that holds dragged files in a floating drop area so you can carry content between windows without opening them side by side.
summary.what_it_does: DropPoint lets you drag files or folders from the system into its window, then drag them out at a different location later. This avoids needing two windows open side by side. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS. When you close it, it minimises to the system tray, and you can reopen it from there. A keyboard shortcut (Shift + Caps Lock on Windows and Linux, Shift + Tab on macOS) opens a new DropPoint instance at the mouse location. The README says the app is meant to work across maximized windows and across virtual desktops or workspaces. Windows needs one extra setting for the window to appear on all desktops.
use_cases: temporarily hold files while navigating folders
quick drop zone for files on desktop
how_to_run: Download the installer for your OS from the Releases Page (Windows zip, macOS dmg, Linux AppImage/deb/tar.gz/rpm)
Developer setup: install Node.js 22 LTS and Git
git clone the repository and cd into DropPoint
notable: Works on Windows, Linux and macOS
Shift + Caps Lock (Shift + Tab on macOS) summons a new instance at the mouse location
Minimises to system tray and can be reopened from there
Inspired by the Dropover app on macOS
Linux users can install via AppImage, deb, tar.gz or rpm
caveats: Minimum OS versions: Windows 10, macOS 12 Monterey, modern 64-bit Linux; older releases before 1.3.x are needed for legacy systems
On Windows, cross-desktop stickiness requires a manual setting in Task view
macOS install requires approving the app under System Preferences > Security & Privacy
Developer setup requires Node.js 22 LTS specifically, as newer releases reportedly break Electron's install
keywords: move files without side by side windows
